page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-128 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an Arm-based Ampere AmpereOne processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 16 vCPUs, executing at one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for system and application data persistence. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated core assignment avoids noisy-neighbor contention inherent in hyperthreaded execution environments.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-128 delivers strong resource density for workloads demanding substantial memory buffers without excessive compute core overprovisioning. The platform is well suited for in-memory caching systems, distributed data analysis, Arm64 continuous integration builds, and memory-intensive application backends.
